The word of God contains banquets: some stronger, such as the Law and the Gospel; others more agreeable, such as the Psalms and the Song of Songs, 1251, 17. The books of the heavenly Scriptures are good pastures, 1140, 2. Eat their food daily, so that you may not hunger but be filled, 1251, 19. They are crumbs, 1474. God filled them with saving commandments by which the soul’s weakness might be healed, 818, 7. They are the remedy for all weariness and the one refuge in temptations, 644, 18. Some are prophetic terrors, others apostolic persuasions; yet in both there is the discipline of one word, 1499, 21. First the Prophet is read, then the Apostle, and so the Gospel, in which there are lucid words and stronger commandments, 1187, 10. If someone seeks there the things that philosophers consider marvelous, he will find them, 1261, 1. The Devil often prepares a snare for the faithful from the Scriptures themselves and makes heretics, 1340, 26.

**SEBASTIAN**, a native of Milan, suffered martyrdom at Rome, 1234, 44.

**SHEM, HAM, AND JAPHETH** signify good, evil, and what is indifferent, 228, 3.

**SEEDS** never properly degenerate, 49, 43.

A seminal power is inherent in things that are born, 45, 33.

**OLD AGE** is sweeter in good morals, more useful in counsels, more prepared for steadfastly undergoing death, and stronger for restraining desires, 18, 31. It ought to be a harbor, not the shipwreck of the former life, 475, 41. Youth is good, but old age is better—and why? 804, 60.

The **SENSES** of human beings, although shared with beasts, nevertheless surpass theirs, 139, 67. Their origin is the brain, 137, 61. Virtue is in the head, 1161, 12. There are two kinds of our senses: one tamed and gentle, the other untamed, which rushes toward irrational bodily pleasures, 206, 4. The bodily senses are regarded as resembling doors, 253, 61. As death enters through our senses, so does life, 1038, 20.

Why people uselessly build costly **TOMBS** after death, 407, 44.

**BURIAL** of the dead is the most excellent service, 592, 5.

The **SERAPHIM** appeared when he wished, 1275, 26.

Silken garments and coverings woven with gold, with which the body of a rich dead person is surrounded, are losses to the living, not aids to the dead, 566, 3.

What does **LATE** properly signify? 1537, 152.

Why is the **SNAKE** so called? 98, 46. Nothing is to be criticized in the fact that the Creator mixed snakes and other poisonous creatures among his creatures, 126, 38. We must not condemn their creation, 147, 7. God did not make the snake for the purpose of causing harm; rather, he showed what it would become, 179, 74. The flesh of a snake is burned, and from its ashes theriac is prepared, 818, 8. If a snake tastes the spittle of a fasting person, it dies, 123, 28. There is a famous saying that a snake, approaching the waters, mates by hissing with a female serpent, in a union during which the snake’s head is cut off, 818, 8. The snake in paradise was not generated without God’s will, 148, 9. How did it express the mystery of faith in paradise? 818, 9. It was a figure of pleasure, 149, 11; 737, 1. Its condemnation is explained, 179, 74. See **ADAM** and **EVE**. The bronze serpent was a figure of Christ, 1037, 15.

**SERTORIUS** and **LEPIDUS** were rebels, 934, 21.

We owe the observance of **SERVITUDE** to the eternal Author by the very law of nature, 784, 16. It is a consoling servitude to serve either just persons, 1123, 31. Wretched is the servitude whose right is uncertain, 1496, 6. It is the price paid for freedom, 768, 5. Nothing is so characteristic of it as always to fear, 491, 20. Glorious is the servitude in which Christ also served for us; blessed is the servitude in which you too serve, 994, 6. Servitude under Christ is precious, and freedom is glorious, 448, 11. How useful is religious servitude to God, 178, 72. Precious is the servitude that is sustained at the expense of virtues, 1174, 15. Everything that imposes servitude upon the soul is useless, even if it lacks no effect, 209, 9.

Many **SLAVES** are freer than their masters, 490, 20. It is not accidental condition that makes a slave, but disgraceful foolishness, 463, 12. The quarrels of slaves should be avoided, not despised, 286, 10. For slaves, being banished to little farms is harsher than being beaten with whips, 699, 67. Punishment is decreed for slaves, grace is bestowed upon free people, 679, 11. A servant of the Lord cannot at the same time be a servant of sin, 1180, 34.

The **SEVERITY** of God is toward a few, his goodness toward all, 1081, 7. See **GOD**.

By the name **SICERA**, the Hebrews call every drink that intoxicates, 552, 54.

**SHECHEM**, according to the Latin interpretation, means “shoulder” or “neck,” 316, 8; 486, 9.

There are no evil or harmful **SIGNS** in heaven, 70, 17.

Christ placed his **SIGN** on the foreheads of individuals; there too Antichrist will place his signs, so that he may recognize his own, 648, 27.

**SILENCE** is useful for everything, and in what way, 847, 13. Divine oracles are customarily revealed especially to those sitting alone, 982, 4. Silence is both safe and decorous; it preserves caution with dignity, 844, 5. It is a strong shield of vigilant defense and the firmest foundation of stability, 842, 2–3. David defeated his adversaries by remaining silent; and because he became like a mute, he recovered his voice, 837, 47. Even if the word of God is within you, you will remain silent in God’s word, and in silence you will cry out so as to be heard by Christ, 845, 8. Silence itself is a medicine, while excessive readiness in speech wounds more swiftly, 834, 42. Above the foundation of virtue, the voice is secure; without a foundation, it is slippery, 843, 4. The virtue of keeping silent is rarer than that of speaking, 1497, 10. Whoever is quick with words empties his inward self and is flooded by outward passions, 1014, 17. The Devil seeks sound; Christ seeks silence, 930, 11.

The blessing of **SIMEON** is explained, 516, 10 ff. In him there is an example of vengeance for violated modesty, 1332, 47. The scribes descended from his tribe, 517, 13.

**SIMONY.** The exercise of priestly ministry ought to be offered freely, 1498, 17. God’s grace is not assessed at a price, nor is profit sought in the sacraments, but the priest’s service, 1348, 51. Those who traffic in the grace of the Holy Spirit cannot have fellowship in the Church of God, 1499, 19. The guilt of selling the mystery is inexpiable, and the heavenly vengeance for grace passes on to descendants, 1348, 53.

**SIMPLICITY** is sought; ambition is not desired, 1299, 53. Nothing is more precious, nothing richer, than simplicity, 963, 21. No fruit is sweeter, 769, 9. In its union with truth, it is sublime in humility itself, 1485, 60. It ought to be cautious, provident, and spiritual, 781, 10. Amid the cunning of this world and the waves of secular desires, it usually finds a harbor only slowly, 255, 64.

What does pagan history relate about the **SIRENS**? 918, 73.

We have chosen **SOBRIETY**, through which Jacob found the birthright that he did not possess, 932, 14. We must be not merely sober but justly sober, 1101, 43. Frugality has killed no one; thrift has harmed no one, 192, 18. By luxuriating we make ourselves members of sin, but by sobriety members of righteousness, 856, 34.

**SUCCOTH** means “tabernacle,” 1019, 5.

**SOCRATES** could have read the writings of Moses, or learned them from others who had read them, 236, 24.

The **SUN** is a creature, not God, 63, 1 ff. It was created by the Son of God, 64, 5. How much superior God is to it, 63, 2. Whether it is fiery by nature, 29, 14; 66, 9. Why it is called the great luminary, 74, 25. From where its greatness may be established, 75, 27. How it is in command of the day, 65, 7. Its globe is neither nearer nor farther from anything, 74, 25. Certain signs are gathered from it, 67, 12.

God’s judgment has generally excluded every increase upon the **PRINCIPAL**, 608, 52; 610, 57 ff. See **USURY**.

Those who make eunuchs out of human beings are rebuked, 83, 9.

The person who **HOPES** desires and loves what he hopes for, 1080, 3. Who can hope beyond hope? 1164, 22. Near hope gives strength, 1103, 3. The strength of our hope, and a certain authority of the one who hopes, is confidence, 1165, 28. We must always hope, ibid. We must not despair of the Lord’s mercy, and why? 838, 51. A person does not seem to be human unless he hopes in God, 356, 1. By how many titles of indulgence has God urged us to hope for forgiveness? 1185, 6. The more serious things the righteous person endures, the more he hopes, 1214, 20. He always adds hope to hope, 1215, 21. Even if you are crushed, even if you are afflicted, even if you waste away through illness, nevertheless wait for the Lord, and hope will not put you to shame, 811, 74. How can one be troubled in whom hope of the heavenly kingdom rises? 1245, 21. In the time of our humility, hope is consoling, 1045, 7. When we are anxious and worried, may hope strengthen us through expectation of future things, 642, 12. We must hope more greatly in divine mercy when human aids have failed, 103, 57. We burden the one in whom we say we have had the greatest hope or confidence all the more if afterward he disappoints our expectation, 875, 21. It seems harsh to purchase hope through dangers, 1411, 1. Despair is fuel for sluggishness, but hope is an incentive to labor, 994, 3.

The Greeks call the portions of the sun’s unmoving sphere *μοῖραι* (*moirai*), 68, 14.

The **SPIRIT** received also from the Son, 1487, 66. The Son proceeds from the Father, and the Spirit proceeds from him, 958, 9. What the principal Spirit is, 700, 72 ff. What the upright Spirit is, 698, 66. When the Holy Spirit is poured into someone, there is a fullness of great virtues, 1277, 34. See **TRINITY**.

The **SPIRIT** in a human being, 83, 10–11.

Wolves flee the leaves of **SQUILL**, 123, 9.

The **STAR** was a figure of Christ, 123, 9.

The glorious **MARTYRDOM OF STEPHEN**, 85, 16. That first martyr had a treasure in his mouth when he spoke of Christ during his passion, 1354, 75. Why God appeared to Adam walking but to Stephen standing, 931, 13. Was he crowned by martyrdom because he saw Jesus standing? 962, 18.

From where did the **STOICS** draw the opinion of their doctrine, “All things belong to the wise person”? 328, 37.

What are the **ELEMENTS** (*Στοιχεῖα*, *stoicheia*)? 40, 18.

The **STOLE** is spiritual clothing and a wedding garment, 1466, 231. It is the insignia of marriage, 1504, 39.

The **STOMACH** is conscious of the head’s secrets and shares in its compassion, 236, 23.

A **FOOL** is one who understands nothing and understands foolish things, 950, 17.

Why do **STARLINGS** feed on hemlock, and why does it not harm them? 48, 39.

**SUBJECTION** to God is good, not degraded or base, but glorious and exalted, 783, 16. Subjection makes minds diligent in service, 1122, 27. The one who wishes to have others subject is himself subjected first, 1126, 39. See **CHRIST**.

**SUBSOLANUS**, the subsolar region, 831, 35.

What and how great a vice is **PRIDE**? 1904, 34 ff. It was the cause of the Devil’s sin, 1040, 8. Pride is the greatest sin in a human being, and why? 1046, 8–9. It first cast down the human being, 1147, 20. It must be avoided, since it overthrows even in prosperity, 776, 26. It does not know how to stand; and if it falls, it does not know how to rise again, 777, 29. To give testimony is a matter of truth; not to shrink from the merit of exaltation belongs to one who boasts, 795, 40. You should do nothing merely to display virtue through contemplation, 1339, 18. Everyone who exalts himself, even if he speaks truly, gives offense, 1005, 36. All wickedness is harsh and uncivilized, and it is inflated by a kind of airy swelling, 264, 87. Christ humbled himself in order to erase the fall of your pride, 1226, 17. Truth is the adversary of pride, 1485, 60. Truth is the adversary of pride, 1485, 60.

A description of the **PROUD**, 250, 54. Why is every proud person unclean in the sight of the Lord? 1167, 31. The heart of the saints is subtle; the heart of the proud is congealed, 1085, 19.

The beauty and usefulness of the **EYEBROWS**, 136, 58; 235, 18.

**PUNISHMENT.** Why do you demand that those things be long-lasting for punishment which cannot be long-lasting for your use? 1343, 33.

**SULLA** stirred up civil wars against the victorious Marius, 934, 21.

The **SYNAGOGUE** has neither beginning nor end, 1222, 3. Christ was its head, 912, 62. It was the first congregation made by God, 984, 9. Afterwards it was abandoned, and why? ibid. It married the Law; when the Law died, it ought to have married the Gospel, 911, 61. As long as it flourished, the Church labored; its decline is the Church’s strength, 1396, 57. As its structure is dissolved, the Church rises, 1505, 6. The Lord abandoned the Jews, and immediately ruin followed the Synagogue, 931, 13. Whoever believes is no longer a fruit of the Synagogue but of the Church; nor is one who is reborn in the Church born from the Synagogue, 1452, 172. No one passes from the Church to the Synagogue without danger to salvation, 1395, 52. How aptly it may be compared to a fig tree, 1449, 161 ff. Its mysteries seem to be expressed by many in the Song of Songs, 984, 9. How did the Lord condemn the adulterous ways of the Synagogue? 779, 6. Cain was its figure, 185, 5. See **CHURCH** and **GOSPEL**.

The **MUSTARD SEED** is Christ, 1454, 182 ff.

## T
TACTUS: We usually test by touch what we cannot test with our eyes, 138, 64. Ταπείνωσις (*tapeínōsis*) is called both the humility of virtue and the humility of affliction, 1224, 10. TAU, in Latin interpretation, signifies “he erred” or “he brought to completion,” 1246, 1. TAURINI: an intake of blood is fatal to a human being, 48, 41. TEMPERANCE is the forerunner of correction and the teacher of discipline, 446, 5. It cuts away desires, 446, 8. The TEMPLE built by Solomon was a type of the Church, 1311, 89. In the temples of God the remains of the faithful are laid to rest for the Lord, 308, 80. TIME comes from this world, not before the world, 10, 20. At least divide your time between God and the world, 1218, 32. In comparison with the eternal light, all things are darkness, 926, [Col. 2290] 2. We read “the darkness of the heart” almost everywhere as referring to sin, 920, 79.

The distinction between TEMPTATION and testing, 304, 66. When is the mind tested? 318, 13. The devil tempts in order to investigate; he investigates in order to tempt, 1339, 19. He tempts in order to overthrow; God tempts in order to crown, 304, 66. The enemy is present, always lying in wait; and if you do not see him, he is present; and if you do not feel him, he attacks, 844, 7. The adversary would not assail the substance of the soul unless he had received power from the Lord, 855, 32. No one can depart from the course of this life without temptation—and why? 1393, 39. No one can be free from temptation, 1073, 46. How the whole journey of this life is full of snares, 400, 24. The more righteous someone is, the more the enemy lies in wait for him, 810, 70. The first temptation of human beings: nature, which supplied nourishment, did not prescribe vices, 79, 2. Why God permits the righteous often to be tempted, 678, 9; 917, 71; 1196, 5. Unless a person has been winnowed by temptations, he cannot separate fragile things from himself as one separates chaff, 903, 40. Temptations often arise on account of sin, 1083, 13. Power for a more severe temptation is permitted to our adversaries when more serious guilt is found in the soul, 835, 48. How the rulers of the world sometimes gratuitously, sometimes not gratuitously, persecute you in your own breast, 1239, 6. We are taught that three things in particular are the devil’s weapons: gluttony, boastfulness, and ambition, 1339, 17; 1343, 35. The devil’s temptations are full of deceit, 174, 61. Temptations of words are the greatest, 655, 8. You see a poor righteous person and are tempted; you see a wicked rich person and are tempted—and this weakness spreads among many, 1245, 20. There is a great snare when riches, honors, or the friendship of tyrants are promised, 1153, 35. The human mind is inclined by tiny moments, and through the deceptions of the persuader is frequently driven this way and that, 1337, 10. The diversity of temptations corresponds to the diversity of those who contend, 1344, 39. Many temptations especially emerge during the nighttime, 1072, 45 and following. We must beware lest the hostile hand uproot those whom the divine hand planted in the house of God, 776, 27. The time of temptations is the time of our humility, 1045, 7. How Christ taught us to resist temptations, 191, 16. It belongs to the righteous that, when they see themselves being tempted, they should ask for help, 921, 82. We ought to ask that we undergo those temptations which we can bear, 1345, 42. The hand of the Lord is said to be present where there is temptation in which a human being is assailed by the devil, 824, 21. Whoever has resolved to keep the judgments of God does not fear temptations, 1146, 18. Why we should by no means fear temptation, 1344, 37 and following. How the devil, while tempting the saints of the Lord, makes them better, 904, 40. In temptations there is a torrent of delight in strength, 775, 24. Those who undergo all temptations are owed the rest of paradise, 756, 38. See DEVIL.

The quality and position of the EARTH, 11, 22. How it was invisible, 14, 26; 35, 7; 38, 14; 42, 25. And unformed, 15, 28. It is divided into three kinds: mainland, island, and peninsula, 336, 55. The earth on which we stand is in the hemisphere of heaven, 1120, 20. Geometers estimated the circumference of the earth at one hundred and eighty thousand stadia, 115, 7. Scripture demonstrates that it is impossible to encompass it, ibid. Histories report that most parts of the earth have often been described, 1294, 38. Earth is the smallest portion of the world, 761, 49. We are not inhabitants but resident strangers upon this earth, 330, 41. How great is the earth’s fertility? 46, 35. Before and after the sin of the human being, 49, 45 and 46. Nothing barren produces growth, 47, 39. How it sprouts and bears fruit is described, 46, 34. The fitting order in the earth’s fruitfulness, 49, 42. What is the heavenly earth that does not pass away? 786, 20.

A TESTAMENT is so called because by it an inheritance of goods is transferred, 196, 28. The Old Testament is in type, the New in truth, 197, 28. The Lord Jesus came and brought a new Testament, and what had been old became new: he overturned the understanding according to the letter and established spiritual understanding, 629, 12. In the New Testament we hold the pledge of divine grace, 197, 28. Why the Lord’s Testament is called a song, 1052, 26. See GOSPEL and SCRIPTURE.

THALES said that everything consisted of water, 3, 6. Why the Evangelist inserted the name of THAMAR, the notorious woman, in the Lord’s genealogy, 1319, 17 and following. THEOTIMUS, knowing and deliberate, about to lose his eyes through the impulse of lust, said: “Farewell, friendly light,” 1351, 64. It is said that THERIAC is made from the body of a serpent, 173, 59. THETH, that is, “exclusion,” 1079, 1. THOMAS seems to have doubted not the Lord’s resurrection but the nature of the resurrection, 1540, 169. India was open to him, 934, 21. The fish THYMALLUS receives its name from a flower, 81, 6. Of it the saying was made: “It smells either of fish or of a flower,” ibid. [Col. 2291]

How the cubs of the TIGER may be rescued, 120, 21. The TIGRIS is said to be swifter than all rivers, 151, 17. It flows past the Assyrians, ibid.; 755, 36.

FEAR arises from bodily and material things, 1009, 1. Fear excludes fear, 1241, 10. If the guilty feared nothing, the innocent would always fear, 1175, 18. What punishment is greater than to fear what you cannot avoid and to be unable to escape what you have feared? 769, 8. To fear belongs to virtue, 1076, 55. There is a fear belonging to the saints, 1240, 8. God alone is to be feared, 1436, 110. Those who fear God are both wise and blessed, 1056, 1. To fear Christ is the fear of piety, not of weakness, 1033, 3. The fullness of wisdom is to fear God, 1151, 31. Unless someone fears God, he cannot renounce sin, 6, 12. Fear is the discipline of wisdom, 791, 28. The confidence of one desiring eternal things and the divine fear of one who trembles converge upon the same result, 1240, 8. There is a fear that pierces the flesh, 1169, 40. Contrition of heart and fear of judgment beneficially prick us: they stimulate but do not wound, 1252, 20. From the fear of the Lord there is a certain progress toward the grace of charity, 1237, 56. The golden foundation is fear full of discipline, 1030, 38. It is shaped by wisdom, instructed by understanding, directed by counsel, formed by virtue, governed by knowledge, and adorned by piety, ibid. Unless the fear of the Lord is according to knowledge, it is of no benefit—indeed, it is greatly harmful, 1029, 36, 37.

The mercy of TOBIT is commended, 591, 2 and following. How can the “sons of thunder” be human beings? 412, 5. The history and qualities of the TOPAZ stone, 1182, 41. The Greek letter T signifies three hundred, 287, 15. It is certain that Christ’s cross is signified by three hundred, 276, 123. Three hundred bronze coins signify the emblem of the cross, 1391, 30.

The TRINITY signifies a distinction of persons, unity of power, 774, 22. We consider nothing free and separate from material composition except the substance of the Trinity alone, 338, 58. It alone is unchangeable, 1119, 18. It has nothing prescribed, circumscribed, measured out, or dimensioned, 1286, 13. An evident testimony for proving the Trinity coeternal and perfect, 1346, 45. This one statement destroys the devices of all heretics: that we should believe the Trinity to be of one power, majesty, and virtue, 734, 72. The Trinity has one will, 699, 71. Those who assert one will in the Trinity necessarily assert one power, 1355, 3. If the Trinity is unity, then its greatness is undivided, just as its operation is undivided, 1438, 19. Whence it may be gathered that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit have one kingdom, 958, 8. Although the divinity is indivisible, the person is distinct, 1432, 92. The Trinity can never be separated from itself, 1312, 92. It can be seen in whatever form the will has chosen, not in one formed by nature, 1274, 25. In the creation of the world the operation of the Trinity shines forth, 16, 29. In the mystery of the Trinity there is a threefold wisdom, 1263, 5. The Son of God is of one nature with the Father, 518, 18. In the Father and the Son there is not one person but one substance, 128, 41. The unity of majesty and divinity of the Son with the Father, 155, 26. The Father and the Son are honored under the same name of majesty, 31, 18. Through the unity of light and name, the Father and the Son are both one, 774, 22. Faith makes the Son equal to the Father and professes the same glory of both, 142, 74. Beware of thinking that the Son of God is not first because he is Son, 1285, 12. The Father does not have one will and the Son another, 517, 60. The Son is of the same divinity as the Father, since he is of the same will, 862, 14; 864, 18. Just as the image of God is God, yet there is one God, so the image of divine goodness is good, yet there is one goodness, 1488, 68. It is clear that the Father and the Son have one dominion, 1470, 248. The Father and the Son are of one power, 1341, 27. The Father and the Son have the same glory and the same virtue, 1309, 84. The operation of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit is one, the power of the operation is one, and the majesty of the deeds is one, 729, 6. The unity of operation in the Father and the Son, 852, 24. Why the Father and the Son have one virtue and a common operation, 875, 20. Jesus is seen in the works of the Father, and the Father is discerned in the works of the Son, 1268, 7. The Father is wholly in the Son, just as the Son is wholly in the Father, 943, 18. Divinity alone acts: generation bears witness both to the Father and to the Son, so that nowhere is the Son seen without the Father, nor the Father without the Son, 1286, 12. Whoever separates the Son from the Father does greater injury to the Father, 1033, 3. The Father is distinguished in the Son by the definition of persons and united by the reality of power, 1505, 5. When I say “the Father” alone, I do not separate the Son, 643, 15. How the Father is well pleased in the Son and the Son blesses the Father, 881, 35. Those who come to baptism confess the Trinity—and why? 1488, 67.

What SADNESS is useful to us? 180, 75. The sadness that usually has seriousness as its companion is often more beneficial, 1116, 9. What the procession of the TRIUMPHANTS was formerly like, 1527, 109 and following. Receiving the reward diminishes the fruit of triumph, 288, 17. The TRIUMVIRS passed from enemies into friends and from friends again into hostile disturbances, 934, 21. [Col. 2292]

The irascible faculty (θυμητικόν, *thymētikón*): what is it? 335, 54. The TURTLE-DOVE, lest the wolf attack its young, lays the leaves of the squill over its nest, 123, 29. Its widowhood is praised, 104, 62. Having lost her mate, she does not know how to indulge in intercourse, 1212, 13. The sea-turtle-dove is said to do more harm after death than while alive, 93, 31. Whoever possesses images of a tyrant already conquered and dead is rightly condemned, 853, 27.

U

ULYSSES, hastening homeward after ten years of exile, was delayed by the Lotus-Eaters and the gardens of Alcinous, while the song of the Sirens nearly brought him to shipwreck, 1334, 2. Its SHADOW clings to every body, and in what ways, 19, 3; 66, 11. Why the sun casts smaller shadows at midday, 72, 21. Why they are larger in winter and smaller in summer, 73, 23. A shadow is a kind of salvation, 73, 22. The shadow passes away, not the truth, 1159, 6.

To smell of PERFUME is characteristic of a luxurious person—or perhaps of no human being, 1390, 27. UNITY cannot transgress, 155, 26. It restrains and governs everything, 972, 2.

URIAS is called “my light,” 725, 49. He was killed as a type under the Law, so that the Synagogue might be released from the snares of the Law, 725, 48. The BEAR is said to shape her malformed cubs with her tongue, 119, 18. She heals her wounds with mullein, ibid., 19. The sick BEAR devours ants, 123, 26.

USURY is so called from use, 605, 43. Why the Greeks called usuries τόκους (*tókous*). Whatever accrues to the principal is usury, 607, 49. They call the principal of a loan what is owed, 595, 14. What kind of usury is good and what kind is bad? 805, 62. Where there is the law of war, there is also the law of usury, 608, 51. Lending at interest, by which usuries are sought, is evil, 593 and following. It is prohibited by the prescription of the ancient and divine Law, 606, 46. Those are rebuked who, after giving money to merchants, receive from their profits proceeds as though they were returns from usury, 607, 49. Scripture joined the moneylender with the idolater in order to equate the crime, 609, 52. To demand usury is to suffocate; to lend at interest is to kill a human being, 607, 46. We must beware lest we bind ourselves by another person’s debt, 620, 90. The Lord seeks interest not on our money but on his own, 1494, 93.

The beauty of a WIFE delights a husband less than her virtue and seriousness, 284, 6. No one may know a woman except his wife, 301, 59. Divine law forbids her to be dismissed, 1471, 4 and following. The common opinion of women is now discredited, since they leave an older husband to follow a younger one, 1333, 134. See MARRIAGE and MATRIMONY.

V

VALENTINUS the heretic was wounded, 1480, 41. Vanity belongs to temporal things; truth, to eternal things, 1016, 25. The wise person who recognizes the vanity of this age does not pray for a prolonged enjoyment of this life, 857, 36. Let us turn our eyes away from vanities, lest what the eyes have seen the mind desire, 1026, 27 and following. See WORLD.

The letter VAU: its interpretation is “he is, and no other,” or “and he,” 1033, 1. A VEIN has more blood than spirit, 266, 92. The pulse of the veins is a messenger of illness or health, 141, 73. The VENERARIUM is the place where Christ suffered, 938, 5. Among HUNTERS we find no righteous person in the whole sequence of the divine Scriptures, 1071, 42. We ought not to condemn the creature of any poisonous living thing, 147, 7. Why are deadly and harmful things generated along with useful foods? 47, 38 and following. They were born for our correction, not for our disfigurement, 126, 38. See SERPENT.

The WORD of God is one substantive Word, not many words, 529, 55. “Word of God” is a name of the Father, 896, 19. It is not, as someone says, a work, but one who works, 198, 32. It is life—and why? 793, 34. It is royal, judicial, and full of priestly justice, 361, 14; 423, 14. It is everywhere, 199, 32. Those who denied the Word had no voice, 1159, 6. Whoever sees the Word and is a partaker of the Word is himself also; but whoever does not know the Word does not exist, 812, 78. To know the Word is a greater work than to minister, 1106, 11. The powers of the heavenly Word are pleasing through knowledge, not terrifying through sound and tumult, 930, 10. The Word remains in heaven, because Satan was cast out from there, 1117, 10. The Word of God became everything for us, 927, 4. What is the union of the divine Word with flesh? 726, 51. The Word of God is health, 823, 19. The Word of God kisses us when the Spirit of knowledge illumines our understanding, 975, 5. The kiss of the Word is the light of sacred knowledge, 359, 8. At times the divine Word truly dies for us, 422, 13. One Word is many things, and many words are one, 999, 20. See SON and TRINITY. [Col. 2293]

The WORD first operates inwardly; the service of the voice follows, 1303, 68. Among human beings the word is consecrated by the voice of the teacher, 1305, 73. For me there is no difference in the word where there is no difference in meaning, 1296, 42. We must disregard words and attend to mysteries, ibid. It is a useless word to speak of human works, for which we shall give an account, 1251, 20. If there is danger from a useless word, how much more from a criminal one? 844, 5. We can always cling to the Word of God, by night and by day, if we meditate on God’s law day and night, 876, 23. How we who now live follow the shadow of God’s words, 999, 19. Let us never neglect the word of the Lord, from which comes the origin of all virtues and a certain progression of all works, 1144, 12. The devil is conquered not by a sword but by the Word of God, 845, 7. Everyone who hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it is a debtor, 615, 71. Yet it must be taken away from no one, ibid. and following. There are not many who live by the Word of God, 114, 91. The Word of God is a great light to some and a lamp to others, 1141, 6, 9. The Word of God is the sword of the Holy Spirit, and the sword of the most wicked spirit is an evil word, 788, 24. It is the key of your mouth, 1367, 48. It is a repellent against weariness, 1013, 15. See MEDITATION.

The whole of TRUTH cannot be comprehended here, 999, 19. Now that we do not comprehend certain things, we cannot speak truly about them, 810, 68. How the progression is made from confessing the truth to knowing divine justice, 1238, 57. The soul reaches the throne of truth when it separates itself from this body and is not deceived by the senses, 394, 10. There is danger not only in saying false things but also in saying true things, 990, 25.

Transformations of the INDIAN WORM, 109, 77. WORMS that arise in children’s entrails from indigestion are killed by a more bitter drink, 347, 38. A description of the BAT, 111, 87. Care for softer CLOTHING makes most people effeminate, 1381, 107. Why are the ways of the Lord avoided? 659, 16. Those who SEE something assume its quality, 95, 36. How great is the grace of WIDOWHOOD? 105, 62. If you forced a widow to come forward publicly, you acted most unjustly, since you made her litigate more immodestly than unjustly, 1171, 7. See VIRGINITY.

What are the LORD’S bonds? 1071, 43. What are the devil’s bonds by which he binds us? 1071, 42. In those whom you think should be punished, their committed offenses must be examined more closely, 298, 47. It is good not to return insult for insult but to refute those who insult by silence, 655, 4, 5 and following. It is better to overlook an injury than to avenge it when you rebuke it, 836, 45. A perfect man is not moved by the injury of the pain of revenge, nor does he repay evil in kind, 484, 3. Blessed is the one who can possess such virtue that, when provoked, he does not become angry and, when stirred, does not wish to avenge himself, 835, 45. See CHARITY and ENEMY.

Why Noah planted the VINE before wheat or barley, 271, 108. How suitably the Christian people may be compared with it, 1500, 29. Why God gave WINE, 62, 72. Through wine Noah was exposed to disgrace, although through the flood he had grown to glory, 62, 72. It belongs to the drunkard to swallow all the wine, but the self-controlled person must use a proper measure, 272, 111. See DRUNKENNESS and NOAH.

The offspring of a VIPER tears open its parent, 768, 6. Its crushed mouth is said to do more harm than poison, 93, 31. Why the person of the male asserts dignity in all courts of gender, 1314, 3, 4. The ROD is the insignia of preeminent power and an instrument of the painful exercise of vengeance, 1424, 59. Before Christ’s coming, the grace of VIRGINITY and widowhood had not yet flourished, 1320, 18. Now there are many examples of virginal integrity, 517, 12. What difference there is between the modesty of a woman and that of a virgin, 1285, 9. How much modesty virgins ought to preserve, 312, 93. The modesty of a virgin is tender, and the reputation of chastity slippery, 1281, 1. It belongs to virgins to tremble and fear at every entrance of a man, and to revere every word spoken by a man, 1284, 8. They ought not to linger in public or in the streets, 1288, 21. It is fitting that the more chaste a virgin is, the humbler she should be, 1289, 22. That the Virgin’s birth is not impossible, 105, 65. Where the lilies of virgins are to be sought, 1441, 128. See GIRL.

Remedies of SHRUBS, 47, 37. From where philosophers transferred the beginnings of the CARDINAL VIRTUES, 150, 14. Some have played at the boundaries of virtues amid the gravest crimes, 824, 20. Virtue and pleasure are described under the type of certain women divided by enmities and disagreements, 188, 13. Simplicity should exist without arrogance, charity without envy, and devotion without anger, 1416, 23. Whoever is inflamed by zeal for virtue excludes all delicacies of the belly, 266, 93. The nature of virtue is the same as that of groves, 1336, 8. Virtue is, as it were, a certain material of virtues, 1371, 65. How the righteous person uses virtue as a kind of lookout, 255, 65. Among the lazy there are no insignia of virtue; among the wise they are held in first place, 188, 12. How much more tolerable it is to love virtues, even if you cannot fulfill them, than to hate virtues, which you cannot harm, 826, 25. There is virtue in the speech of the saints, 1107, 12. The fortifications of virtue are eternal, 788, 23. Flight from evils is the likeness of God, and the image of God is acquired through virtues, 397, 17. The virtues are connected and joined to one another, 133, 22. Yet one virtue holds primacy among the saints, 1370, 63. When are the virtues perfect? 208, 8. Glory for virtues is owed to God alone, 799, 50. Under divine instruction the progress of human virtue has grown, 655, 6. The green places of virtues have Christ as their fountain and the abundance of spiritual grace by which they overflow, 327, 34. Christ is the end of all virtues, 1129, 48. Perfect virtues receive the whole inheritance of glory; something inferior is sprinkled upon customary and mediocre virtues, 194, 23. There are crowns for individual virtues, 1161, 11. Virtue alone is the companion of the dead, 1439, 122. Death is cheap, but virtue is precious, 1437, 17. The one whom virtue has carried upon its shoulders cannot die, 1255, 31. Whoever loses what is his own in order to cling to virtue loses what belongs to him and receives what is eternal, 1105, 6. God himself is the perfect reward of virtues, 1059, 11. The Evangelists describe signs of virtue for faith and works of virtue for imitation, 1356, 4. There is never spirit without virtue, nor virtue without spirit, 1278, 36.

LIFE is the enjoyment of the gift of breathing; death is deprivation of it, 389, 2. Our life began from divine inspiration, which is not dissolved, 1091, 15. The goal of this brief labor is near, and the crown of perpetual fruit; the suffering is bearable, the reward immeasurable, 452, 23. Perhaps because of human sins God made the days of this life shorter, although previously it extended to nine hundred and seven hundred years, 851, 21. Life in the body is the shadow and image of life, not the truth, 998, 18. What the true life is, 1032, 46; 1100, 40. To enjoy life is to enjoy good things; death, by contrast, is to be deprived of good things, 389, 2. Life is good—but eternal life, 432, 37. The image of life must be drawn from heaven, 1116, 8 and following. What it means to live life, to die death, to live for death, and to die for life, 264, 44, 45. To live life is more than merely to live, 1004, 33. Our life is either the way of virtue or of iniquity, and one of the two must be chosen, 748, 25. It is tested by fire, just as virtue is approved through contests, 1097, 30. While anyone is in this life, he cannot be praised with a definitive proclamation, 744, 16. Contest is owed, not the prize, 811, 73. This life is not the place of reward, since it is in the place of death, 996, 1. How many living people are in hell, 1253, 24.

The VINE is set before us for imitation, 53, 52. It is praised, 51, 49. It is compared with the Church, 52, 50.

The first VICES to be avoided, 750, 28. Nature gave us the grace of flying; pleasure took it away, 1436, 114. A VOLUNTARY minister has a reward; one who is compelled dispenses obedience, 1148, 24. There is a great difference between someone who does something unwillingly out of necessity and someone who chooses what is good voluntarily, 1402, 80. The Lord approves the spontaneous actions of his servants rather than their compelled actions, 1131, 3. Christ chose a voluntary soldier for himself; the devil buys a voluntary servant for himself, 447, 10. No one is held guilty unless he has turned aside by his own will, 447, 10.

PLEASURE and its arts are elegantly described, 189, 14. How does virtue, under the solicitation of pleasure, devise sounder counsels? 190, 15. How can the pleasure of the flesh be called wise? 169, 54. Christ cuts away natural pleasures, 1469, 1. Why did pleasure seem to the Epicureans to be the highest good? 351, 85. Their opinion is refuted, 314, 3. When the mind’s strength has been relaxed, pleasure pours itself forth, 357, 2. Nothing is enough for extravagant pleasure, 1463, 215. For the sake of the soul’s pleasure, bodily health is generally despised and danger is not avoided, 1351, 64.

A VOW is a petition for good things from God together with a promise to pay the offered gift, 195, 25. Its first grace is the speed with which the promised gift is paid, 197, 29 and following. The usefulness of the VOICE, 139, 67. The voice is the cry of works and of faith, 1280, 41.

The good SCARS OF WOUNDS OF TRIUMPH, by which the victors of this earthly battle glory, 839, 55. A WOUND is of the mind—and how ought it to be healed? 1238, 2 and following. The VULTURE conceives without any seed of a male, 105, 64. It prolongs its life to one hundred years, 105, 64. It is accustomed by certain signs to announce the death of human beings, 110, 81.

X

The history of XENOCRATES, 1182, 41. XENOPHON the Socratic wished to portray the character of the wise man through invented events in the book which he titled Κύρου παιδεία (*Kýrou paideía*, “The Education of Cyrus”), 282, 2.

Z

ZABULON signifies “deliverance from nocturnal things,” 521, 26. His blessing is explained, 521, 26. ZACHARIAH seems to be designated as the high priest and to be a type of Christ, 1273, 22. [Col. 2295] Why ZACCHAEUS received Christ as a guest into the inner house, 1492, 81. ZAIN signifies in Latin “lead yourself” or “here,” 1043, 1. ZARA in interpretation signifies “Dawn” or “East,” 1321, 22. He was a type of Christ, 1324, 29. ZEAL is one thing, and *parazeal* another, 779, 5. There is zeal for life, and there is zeal for death, 1197, 10 and following. Those who have zeal consider everyone who is an enemy of God to be their own enemy—even their father, brothers, and sisters, 1198, 12. ZENO was the teacher of the Stoics and the founder of the sect itself, 328, 37.

[Col. 2296]

INDEX OF WORDS, SENTENCES, MORE DIFFICULT DOCTRINES, AND ANCIENT RITES EXPLAINED IN THE NOTES.

What does *abalienare* mean? 355. From where Ambrose seems to have derived the name Abraham, 313. Whether Abraham may rightly be accused of betraying his wife Sarah’s chastity, 285. *Absolvo*, that is, “I conclude and prove,” 824. What does *abstemius* signify? 1223. *Acerbo*, or better *acervo*, that is, “I exaggerate,” 267. What does *acroama* signify? 34. *Acta*, *actae*: what are they? 93. *Actor agri*, that is, a country steward, 287. Adam. Christ leaps over Adam, 1034. *Adipsal* is said from *adeps*, “fat,” 665. “To inflame lusts,” 17, 1038. Ἀδολεσχῆσαι, that is, “to hallucinate,” 1013. Who were the advocates or registered persons? 1063. Whether Ambrose believed adultery to have been prohibited before the law of Moses, 289. Ἀὲρ for ἔαρ, “springtime,” 263. How many peoples can this air support? 568. *Aethiopes mercatus* is used in place of *Aethiopici*, 827. Who was the *agonothetes*? 550. *Albae* or *albulae*, 53. What is *albugo*? 592. The earth itself could not contain Alexander, 953. To flee what is another’s, 440. He cites Paul, 507. To engage in conversation with the flesh, 975. Amalek, by interpretation, is understood as “king of the wicked,” 7. Whether Ambrose suffered a lapse of memory, 476. He delivered a sermon among the catechumens at the feast of Epiphany, 1354. How it should be understood that the people conferred the priesthood on Ambrose, 1490. Whether the second *Apology of David* is genuinely Ambrose’s work, 703. See David. What is *amiantus*? 541. To drink *amystide*, 555. Ammaon and Cleophas, disciples, 723, 1542. What is an *anaboladium*? 520. Who are the *anaglypharii*? 605. Whether Ananias and Sapphira were condemned to eternal death, 1197. *Ancylae*: the bends or curves of the elbow or leg, 124. Before inflicting death on the emperor Gratian, Andragathius took care that he should be led to Maximus, 964. When the angels were created, 737. Whether they see God, 1274. What Ambrose thought about their fall, 231, 677, 1011. The irrational soul, 1460. The higher faculties of the soul, 338. What dwellings the soul has after death, 385. Whether after the end of this life it is still held in uncertainty regarding the future, 409. The Apollinarists are rebuked, because they maintained that Christ’s divinity had suffered, 1515. The apostles are named simply and without an added designation, 755. Apostolic food, 1165. What is an apostrophe? 964. He counts storehouses, 750. What is an apse? 849. The unfortunate outcome of the Council of Ariminum, 1372. Judge and warrior, 832. The devices of argument, 794. Arius. Because of him Christ reigns, 1355. Aspendius the harpist, 742. The appointed athlete, 800. Athletic banquets, 1124. With no touch, that is, gradually and imperceptibly, 1037. What does *averruncare* signify? 939. An august definition, that is, an imperial enactment, 1232. The pious bird, that is, the stork, 120. Austrigo, *ustrigo*, that is, “burning,” 49. Auxentius is designated as an Arian, 1422. The cruel law written by him is called a sword, 1423. The nut-tree rod seen by Jeremiah, 856. What is Bethel? 318. For Ambrose Bethlehem is the same as Bethel, 469.

[Col. 2296]

They prepared themselves for the sacrament of baptism by washing, not only with fasts and prayers but also with confession of sins, 383. Immersion of the whole body in baptism, 1177. In what sense do we descend into the Jordan when we are baptized? 966. A baptized person did not offer [the Eucharist] until entering the eighth day, 971. The harmful delay of baptism and penance, 1464. See Sacraments. Who used to grow a beard and let their hair grow long? 1320. Why Baruch is cited under Jeremiah’s name, 199. Blessedness. See Soul. What the blessings or beatitudes signify, and when they were sung in churches, 1217. The *bravium* is a crown or prize of victory made from the branches of various trees, 57. Gills in fish, 83. What does *bruchus* signify? 63. They covered the belt with golden bosses, 549. Corpses burned among the Greeks and Romans, 981. The harmony and concord of the heavens, 377, 738. The substance of the heavenly powers, 886. Whether Cain was killed by Lamech, 1475. Calligonus the eunuch, censured by Ambrose, 496. What “to sing within” means, 741. Singing in the Church. See Gospels and Psalms. To catch an unwary person, 283. Capital punishment, 1221. To decide concerning a capital matter, 596, 1065. *Capite minutus*, that is, degraded from the rank of nobility, 601. *Castimonium* for *castimonia*, 285. What are the *catadupa*? 25. The catechumens gave their names twice, 1354. Their ranks, 545. The salt of the catechumens, 1513. *Censio*, that is, censure and moderation, 313. Roman censorial discipline, 1293. What is a census? 1171. *Cernimus*, *decernimus*, that is, “we serve as soldiers,” 435. *Centrum*, that is, a goad or dart, 5. What is the *centesima*? 466. According to popular belief, the stag mates at the beginning of the year, 639. In what branches of knowledge were the Chaldeans learned? 1297. What are the claws of crabs? 88. The Christian lacks the privilege, 816. Christ was born from the tribe and seed of Zara, 1327. Why Ambrose discusses his genealogy with such care, 1329. That he assumed all the marks of human—but harmless—emotions, 899. His soul as the administrator of a temporary dispensation, 957. His subjection laid aside together with the servitude of his body, 958. The Jews thought he would come from a woman, 1307. Whether he was born in a stable or a rocky cave, 1294. What was his homeland? 1346. He allowed his body to be stoned, 828. In what part of the world was he crucified? 158. He suffered in the *venerarium* [reading uncertain], 938. And on the great Sabbath, 1476. From what tribe were his persecutors? 472. Whether in his death his divinity was separated from his body or soul, 1531. How the three days of his death are to be explained, 915. He is held by the price of sin, 489. How the sin of the world could have been abolished in no other way than by his blood, 942. He naturally possessed the power to forgive sins, 1285. Ambrose attributes to Christ what properly belongs to the Word, 1207. Christ is called “faith,” and for what reason, 412. The circus games and theatrical spectacles, 1025. *Clindiae*, or *clindia*, 554. *Coccus* is used in Scripture for fire, 1201. Codrus, the last king of the Athenians, 1409. “Know yourself”: and who was the author of this saying? 985. *Collatio*, that is, the distribution of collected money, 870. What does *colludium* signify? 978. What is a *collyrium*, and how was it made? 1000. “Heavenly records” has the same meaning as the book of life, 250. In Scripture *commune* has the same meaning as “polluted,” and the verb *communico* likewise means “to pollute,” etc., 163, 681. The community of nature, 456.

[Col. 2297]

Κόνδυ is a kind of measure, 822. External and verbal confession of sins, 1465. Its necessity, 1523. See Baptism and Penance. Who are called confessors, and why are violets assigned to them? 1441. To flee from a crime, 419. *Conscientia*, that is, knowledge, 923. *Consortium* sometimes means proximity and adjoining houses, 1077. *Conspersio* has the same meaning as confusion, 207. The contagion of polluted flesh, that is, leprosy, 681. *Convenit*, that is, “he prosecutes by judgment,” 977. Banquets over the tombs of martyrs, 533, 553. How great was the reverence once shown, even among barbarians, for the table and the fellowship of banquets? 875. It was the custom of the Thracians to fight during meals, 548. The Olympic crown, 41. The green crown, 1026. A horn full of wine, 549. *Crimen*, that is, accusation, 392. What do *cromata* signify? 34. What were the curiae? 1314. What sort of contest was the curule contest? 689. The swanlike grace of old age, 804. Dallaeus is criticized, 969, 973. What does the name David signify? 720, 39. In the second *Apology of David* the truth of his adultery is not destroyed, 721. To throw down from a wall, 399. Depending upon our judgment, 857. *Depositus*, that is, despairing, 101. What does diverting blame mean? 219. How is Jacob said to have possessed the kinds of definitions? 437. *Despicere* sometimes has the same meaning as *dispicere*, “to inspect and consider,” 361. *Devotio*, that is, obedience in carrying out God’s commandments, 280. God is Lord not by the addition of a person but by the totality of nature, 1495. The devil’s judgment postponed, 1228. What is a *diapsalma* in the Psalms? 851. *Dictamnum*: what herb is it, and where does it grow? 123. *Dictio* sometimes has the same meaning as oracles, 886. *Disputatio* often has the same meaning as treatment or evangelical preaching, 1494. The order of disputation is the order of treatment, 1408. *Distrinximus*, or *distinximus*, 680. Whether divorce was prohibited by human law, 1471. Doctrine has the same meaning as discipline and instruction, 185. Legitimate deceit, 461. The *dorcadion* has especially keen sight, 1035. The punishments of the rich banqueter, 1228. What is a diptych? 88. An *echidna* or *echinna* is a female viper, 604. The Church does not know how to publish its laws, 420. Whether the ecclesiastical book is authentic, and who its author was, 807. The book of Ecclesiastes is attributed to Solomon, 606. It is designated by the phrase “In the Canticles,” 831. He deserved an edict, 591. The merit of exaltation, 496. Election was achieved by the one who heard the caller and received the one who came, 905. Heavenly beings supplied Elijah’s food, 792. Whether Elimas, called Barjesus in Acts XIII and elsewhere Barjeu, should also be called Hymnus, 77. Unburnable lampwicks, 541. Emblems are figures and ornaments added to some vessel, 594. *Enchoria*: native and local birds, 99. An epilogue, that is, a complaint, 121. Ἐπινίκιος, a hymn of victory, 841. The privileges of bishops toward prisoners, 1071. They had the right not only to admonish but also to restrain, 1490. The ancient custom of celebrating the consecration of bishops annually, 1489. *Eruditio* sometimes has the meaning of correction by blows, 1145. Whether Isaiah died after being cut into two parts, 1123. Whether the Fourth Book of Ezra is apocryphal, 387. That the Gospels and lessons in church were not sung but read, 763. The pseudo-Gospel of the Twelve, 1265. The pseudo-Gospel of Basilides, 1265. Several pseudo-Gospels under the names of various apostles, 1265. Various heretics corrupted the Gospel texts, 1266. Heresy composed many Gospels, 1473.

The Eucharist is called “the sacrament” by antonomasia, 696. Knowledge of the mysteries, and especially of the Eucharist, was concealed from catechumens, 546. It is the true sacrifice, 1275. Christ’s blood in the Eucharist is called a rose, 1139. The custom of receiving it only on an empty stomach, 1073.
